Cheng Li: starting a thread to capture the validation procedure we ran on the prod-trace replay harness. want to make sure the anonymization + sampling steps are deterministic and don't bias kernel selection metrics
Maria Gonzalez: thanks. what were the exact flags used for the run?
Cheng Li: replay.sh --trace /mnt/traces/2026-03-01.log --anon-mode hashpad --sample 0.03 --seed 1337 --preserve-kv-order --kernel-policy auto
Eli Thompson: two quick notes: 1) hashpad anonymization pads prompt lengths to multiples of 8 which skewed batching distribution in the first run; 2) sample fraction 0.03 gives very few long-seq examples so tail latency was noisy
Samir Patel: saw that too. parity checker reported mismatches on 12 traces, mostly when kernel-policy switched to matmul-fused on certain seq_len buckets
Maria Gonzalez: can you paste the parity diff summary?
Cheng Li: parity-summary (run id r-2026-03-12-09):
```
total_traces: 8123
parity_failures: 12
failure_types: [kv_miss_divergence x5, rng-seed-mismatch x3, kernel-quant-band x4]
kv_hit_rate: 0.921
mean_latency_root: 23.4ms
mean_latency_replay: 23.6ms
```
Eli Thompson: rng-seed-mismatch is the scary one. replay harness uses two RNGs: one for sampling and another inside matmul kernels when using fp16 stochastic rounding. need to lock both
Infra Ops: infra note — the worker image used was gcr.io/redwood/replay:2026-03-09, which included a kernel upgrade (cuBLAS-like kernel v2.1)
Samir Patel: that aligns. the kernel upgrade introduced non-deterministic batched GEMM for small N which explains kernel-quant-band mismatches
Maria Gonzalez: proposed mitigation checklist: 1) force deterministic kernels for parity runs (--kernel-policy deterministic) 2) increase sample to 0.1 for better tail coverage 3) run anonymization audit (hashpad vs truncation) 4) lock RNG seeds across all components 5) add kv-warmup phase to the harness
Cheng Li: implemented 1,3,4 locally and re-ran on a 1000-trace slice. new result: parity_failures: 0, kv_hit_rate: 0.88, but batching distribution changed (more groups of 8)
Eli Thompson: batching change is expected because anonymization padding altered seq_len histogram. need an apples-to-apples compare: run two replays on identical trace set, one with hashpad anonymization and one with a masking-only anonymizer that preserves lengths
Samir Patel: agreed. i ran that yesterday at small scale:
```
# preserve-len run
replay.sh --trace slice-1000.log --anon-mode mask-only --sample 0.05 --seed 42 --kernel-policy deterministic
# pad run
replay.sh --trace slice-1000.log --anon-mode hashpad --sample 0.05 --seed 42 --kernel-policy deterministic
```
Samir Patel: result summary: mask-only mean_latency 22.8ms, hashpad mean_latency 24.1ms, kv_hit_rate mask-only 0.90, hashpad 0.86
Maria Gonzalez: that suggests anonymization padding is the main driver of latency and KV hit regression in these parity-focused runs
Cheng Li: action items drafted:
- infra to provide pinned worker image with deterministic kernels (Infra Ops)
- dev-runtime to add explicit RNG locking at harness boundary (Eli)
- dev-qa to run apples-to-apples anonymizer comparison at 10k traces and capture seq_len histograms + batch size distribution (Maria)
- replay infra to add kv-warmup option and measure hit-rate impact (Samir)
Eli Thompson: for the RNG locking i propose we set env REPLAY_RNG_SEED and also pass --deterministic-rng to the internal kernel layer. patch ready, will open PR today
Infra Ops: pinned image created: gcr.io/redwood/replay:deterministic-2026-03-12 sha:sha256:abc123def
Maria Gonzalez: qa run scheduled for 3/14 08:00 UTC, i'll collect profiling traces (nvprof and internal counters) and attach to the run id
Cheng Li: one more check: we should also log which kernel variant was chosen per-request in the replay metadata so that later we can correlate parity failures to kernel selection heuristics
Samir Patel: good point — added metadata field kernel_variant to replay payload in latest commit
replay-bot: scheduled job r-2026-03-14-08 for apples-to-apples anonymizer test. results will post to #eng-runtime when done :robot_face: 
Maria Gonzalez: thanks everyone. next sync after the 10k run. if parity failures pop up again, we'll attach minimal repro and escalate to kernel team
Eli Thompson: adding note: if deterministic run still shows small quant-band diffs, we may need to force reference matmul path for verification (even if it's slower)
Cheng Li: agreed. documented in the run playbook. closing this mini-thread, will post the run ids and links in the follow-up
